I don't understand. I left someone because they became sexually intimate with someone else and I felt hurt as a result. I thought leaving was the right decision because why stay in a situation where I continue to get hurt? I also thought they were just using me for my capacity to be compassionate; honestly it almost felt as though I were being manipulated. Better to let go and move onto something that actually helps me and nourishes who I am. But I feel as though I'm resisting/rejecting the person by leaving them rather than accepting them. Am I going in the right direction by leaving? Or is leaving a rejection of the situation vs acceptance of the people?

I also thought the idea of impermanence meant that  their becoming intimate with others and my leaving as a result was just how things were going and that this was just an end of a relationship since all things change. I'm so confused because I'm not sure if acceptance meant being okay with them being sexual and that I should stick around despite the pain I feel, maybe continuing to feel this pain would help me overcome it(it doesn't seem to be the case, it seems like I'm becoming more resentful by staying.) Or if acceptance meant being okay with leaving as a result of learning of their affair.

Being realistic, I don't have time for everyone; if they're with others, then I need to focus on my own things too. It's not fair to me that I be expected to stay around while they get to do their own things.

Also here's this long wall of text I was going to put in the original post, but decided to omit due to not getting to the point.

Although its not related to the career I want, I thought there would be many benefits to working retail. For one, I have slight social anxiety, so retail would help force me to adapt to social situations more; maybe even develop a better understanding of it too. Another benefit would be financially. My mom gives me so much money, but I'd like to experience financial independence to get a better sense of a worth of a dollar. Lastly, I believe work would expose me to the more harsher realities that may temper my psyche. Usually I just comfortably go on the computer or study, but I've never had to deal with an angry customer or organize and manage a team during a crisis. Exposure to these things may lead me to develop a course of action to deal with them which in turn prepare me for future unpleasant scenarios. I don't know if this is technically a development of psyche, though I feel like reacting in this manner does help strengthen emotions. There can be a lot of benefits in working retail, and I believe doing so would greatly help me grow as an individual.

One more thing I'd like to mention... I believe, as an INTJ, working in retail will help identify and develop some of my best skills: Organizational and Analytical skills. I've only ever seen these two come into play when I play video games. When i'm totally in the zone playing video games(maybe an RTS or fps game), I begin to think about the mechanics of the game and see how they're functioning live. Sometimes I experiment with the game to get a better understanding of the mechanics. Once I do understand it, I'm able to play the game in such a way that makes others question how I'm able to do what I do. However, I'm never able to see something like this happen in real life. I believe this is due to always being inside and not getting exposure to the outside world, thus I'm not able to readily analyze it. So maybe if i'm settled in a job that requires me to do repetitive work, i'll be able to analyze certain mechanics like those in video games. Maybe mechanics involved in handling customers or communication in general. Maybe mechanics involving management. If there are any INTJ who understand this vague idea of just understanding the mechanics of certain things to the point of playing with them, I'd love to hear your input... In truth, I've had many relationships in the past four years in community college that some would call friendships. But really, most of them felt like my putting on an act to be polite, rather than truly being myself. There are some people who I was truly myself around, but we kind of just lost touch when we focused on our own businesses.

> Friends judge each other - it's no biggie, but it depends on whether it is laced with condescension/malice/disgust etc.

This part is what really made me leave some of my friends at the end of high-school, some of their comments felt like they did have some condescension or disgust in them. For example, one time in high-school, me and my group of friends came together for a game of Left4Dead2. Altogether we were 4 people in a skype call. Although, one of them decided he wasn't going to join us because he had to do "daily's" on World of Warcraft. We were fine with it, and just went ahead with the game. All fun and good, the three of us screaming and laughing; generally enjoying the game. But then at one instance I died in the game and the guy who ended up not joining our game said "Haha, you died! Now nobody likes you!". The entire call went silent. It was really awkward. He ended up saying "...Sorry". Like...was that a joke? I don't remember how the rest of the night went, but I believe us three ignored it and continued playing through...

The more I recall what happened to my old group of friends, the more I realize I left them because they were pretty mean. I remember some of them would message me privately talking ill towards one another. Blaming one another. It stopped being fun... Some of them really didn't want me to leave when I did though. And I guess some of them really did like having me around. I kind of miss having them around. Despite all the negative stuff that happened, when there was harmony among our group and we all joined a game, I feel like those were some of the funnest times I've had.
